hypothesis: Iter 87 = fix the MEAL-TIMING FRAME BUG in the neural gut, the true root cause of the chronic verifier_cat[meal] failure (the only gate failure left after iter-86 solved glucose_mape/baseline). Background: iter-86 landed with glucose_mape<=0.20, overall 0.0912, hr/overall passing, but gate.passed=False on verifier_cat[meal]=0.53<0.65 (post-meal glucose amplitude ~0.25 mg/dL/g vs the ~0.7 literature target). Diagnosis on iter-86 model.pt: the neural gut computed meal-absorption time-since-meal from ABSOLUTE minute-of-day (precompute_gut_outputs: times=arange*dt+start_time_minutes, then forward_window dt=times-meal.time), but meal.time is a WINDOW OFFSET (0-based, matching the teacher simulate_full_body frame, the benchmark dataset, and every scenario/protocol generator). So absorption was shifted start_time_minutes earlier than the window: an 08:00 start (480) pushed the entire absorption peak OUT of the window and only the dying tail leaked in, crushing the measured meal amplitude. This mis-timing was consistent across training signals AND the benchmark, so iters 68-86 fought the resulting low amplitude with Ra/dose-response/estimator/setpoint hacks that never fully worked. The metabolic machinery is FINE: with meals on the correct clock the model ALREADY produces 0.4-0.74 mg/dL/g dose-scaling peaks (30g exceeds 0.7). FIX (model.py, 2 edits): (1) precompute_gut_outputs uses the window-offset absorption clock (times=arange*dt, no +start_time_minutes, no %1440 wrap) since absorption depends only on minutes-since-meal and start_time_minutes is only the circadian clock used elsewhere; (2) integrate precomputes the gut internally when gut_outputs is None AND meals are present, so the single-embedding benchmark path (batch=1, previously per-step absolute-clock gut) also gets the offset clock. Keeps all iter-86 structure (minimal-model setpoint, b_emb, Sg band, Ra, Si, teacher diversity, leash/clamp). NO metabolic/hyperparameter change; trainArgs identical to iter-86.
expectedEffect: PRIMARY: verifier_cat[meal] clears 0.65. Validated on iter-86 weights as-is: correcting meal timing lifts verifier_cat[meal] 0.657->0.855 over the 24 generated benchmark episodes (deterministic-embedding measurement). With glucose_mape<=0.20, hr, and overall already passing since iter-86, gate.passed should be TRUE. Training also gets correctly-timed meals now (dose_response/cohort/cold_distill/carb_mass_balance all previously mis-timed), so postprandial dose-response and meal-driven cohort statistics train against physiological absorption instead of a shifted tail. WATCH: (R1) meal-driven cohort/dose-response losses shift (meal responses now larger); confirm no fasting-eval baseline regression since eval windows have no meals. (R2) glucose_mape stays <=0.20 (amplitude and fasting baseline are decoupled; eval is fasting). (R3) the gut kernel was learned partly around the bug, so retraining lets it settle on the true absorption shape.
